_comment: weatherbot-narrow-v3 — Context Set for QueryData / Conversational
Analytics API on the weatherbot narrow schema.
Delta from v2 (weatherbot-narrow-v2.json, currently deployed):
* Kept all v2 value_searches (3), facets (20), and templates (17).
* Added 2 templates for 'when was <measurement> at its peak today'
— one location-agnostic, one location-filtered. Both return
`(observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::timestamp AS local_time`
as the FIRST column so the natural-language layer never has to
convert UTC to local. Also both return display_name AND
physical_location so the answer can name the sensor.
Bug motivating the v3 additions (observed 2026-07-06 23:22 PT):
User asked 'what time was the hottest temperature today?'
QueryData generated a SQL that correctly found the 88F Garage
reading at UTC 2026-07-06 23:00 (= 4pm PT today). The result
returned raw observed_at with no local_time conversion, and the
bot narrated 'observed_at = 2026-07-06 23:00 UTC' as '11pm last
night' — straight-through misread of '23:00' as '11pm' without
the -7 hour conversion. The result also returned station.name
('Home2') instead of display_name/physical_location so the bot
couldn't say 'the garage' from the row either.
Cumulative delta from v1 (weatherbot-narrow.json):
Same as the v2 delta plus the v3 additions above. v1 kept in
the repo for reference and as a rollback target.
Empirical grounding for the swim event finder (unchanged from v2):
* 30-min pool temp variation p99 = 1.2°F over 17,108 windows.
* Threshold 1.0°F chosen because a validated swim event
* Time-of-day gate 12:00-20:00 local avoids overnight cover-
induced sensor stability + midday sun-on-probe artifacts.
* Value <= 95 filter excludes Class A artifacts (2026-05-30
had ~8h of readings in the 99-105°F range).
Upload workflow: Cloud SQL Studio -> Data Agents -> Context
Sets -> Upload as weatherbot-narrow-v3 (NEW version, not an
overwrite of v2 — keeps rollback trivial). Then flip
WEATHERBOT_GDA_CONTEXT_SET_ID in infra/env.sh from the v2
resource name to the v3 resource name and redeploy the toolbox
(bash infra/05-deploy-toolbox.sh). To roll back, flip the env
var back to the v2 resource name.

value_searches.description: Fuzzy, case-insensitive match for the place a sensor is installed. Maps the user's spoken word ('pool', 'poul', 'out side') to the actual title-cased enum stored in sensors.physical_location: 'Outdoor', 'Bedroom', 'Garage', 'Pool', 'Pool (retired)'. Critical: WITHOUT this, the planner emits `WHERE physical_location = 'pool'` (lowercase) and silently returns zero rows.
value_searches.query: WITH TrigramMetrics AS (SELECT T."physical_location" AS original_value, (T."physical_location" <-> $value::text) AS normalized_dist FROM "sensors" T WHERE T."physical_location" % $value::text) SELECT original_value AS value, 'sensors.physical_location' AS columns, 'Sensor Location' AS concept_type, normalized_dist AS distance, ''::text AS context FROM TrigramMetrics

value_searches.description: Fuzzy match for what kind of reading the user wants. Maps colloquial words ('temp', 'temperature', 'humid', 'rain', 'wind speed', 'wind gust') to the canonical snake_case enum stored in sensors.measurement_type. Valid values: temperature, humidity, dew_point, feels_like, wind_speed, wind_gust, wind_direction, pressure, rain_rate, rain_total, solar_radiation, uv_index, pm25, aqi, battery.
value_searches.query: WITH TrigramMetrics AS (SELECT T."measurement_type" AS original_value, (T."measurement_type" <-> $value::text) AS normalized_dist FROM "sensors" T WHERE T."measurement_type" % $value::text) SELECT original_value AS value, 'sensors.measurement_type' AS columns, 'Measurement Type' AS concept_type, normalized_dist AS distance, ''::text AS context FROM TrigramMetrics

value_searches.description: Fuzzy match against the human-friendly sensor name (e.g. 'Pool temperature', 'Outdoor humidity', 'Bedroom dew point'). Useful when the user names a specific reading rather than a location + measurement type. Backed by a GiST trigram index on sensors.display_name.
value_searches.query: WITH TrigramMetrics AS (SELECT T."display_name" AS original_value, (T."display_name" <-> $value::text) AS normalized_dist FROM "sensors" T WHERE T."display_name" % $value::text) SELECT original_value AS value, 'sensors.display_name' AS columns, 'Sensor Display Name' AS concept_type, normalized_dist AS distance, ''::text AS context FROM TrigramMetrics

templates.nl_query: What was the highest pool temperature in the last two weeks?
templates.sql: SELECT max(r.value) AS max_value, s.unit FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id WHERE s.physical_location = 'Pool' AND s.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.reliable = true AND r.value <= 95 AND r.observed_at >= now() - interval '14 days' GROUP BY s.unit
templates.intent: What was the highest pool temperature in the last 14 days, excluding suspected sun-on-probe artifacts (above 95F)?
templates.manifest: What was the highest a given measurement at a given location in the last a given number of days?

templates.intent: On how many calendar days in the last 14 days did the pool temperature exceed 90 degrees (excluding sun-on-probe artifacts above 95F)?

templates.nl_query: When did I go swimming based on pool temperature drops?
templates.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT r.observed_at, r.value FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id WHERE s.physical_location = 'Pool' AND s.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.is_active = true AND s.reliable = true AND r.value <= 95 AND r.observed_at >= now() - interval '60 days'), windowed AS (SELECT observed_at, value, max(value) OVER w AS max_30min, min(value) OVER w AS min_30min, value - first_value(value) OVER w AS delta_from_start FROM base WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY observed_at RANGE BETWEEN interval '30 minutes' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)), dedup AS (SELECT observed_at, max_30min, min_30min, delta_from_start, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY date_trunc('hour', observed_at) ORDER BY (max_30min - min_30min) DESC) AS rn FROM windowed WHERE (max_30min - min_30min) >= 1.0 AND delta_from_start <= -1.0 AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (observed_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles')) BETWEEN 12 AND 19) SELECT (observed_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles')::timestamp AS local_time, round(min_30min::numeric,2) AS min_temp_f, round(max_30min::numeric,2) AS max_temp_f, round((max_30min - min_30min)::numeric,2) AS range_f, round(delta_from_start::numeric,2) AS signed_delta_f FROM dedup WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY observed_at DESC LIMIT 50
templates.intent: Find pool temperature drops of >=1.0F over any 30-minute window in the last 60 days, in the local afternoon (12pm-8pm). Empirically these correspond to swim events (mixing of cooler subsurface water). Excludes readings >95F as sun-on-probe artifacts. Deduplicated to one representative per hour.
templates.manifest: Find pool swim events (temperature drops in the local afternoon) over the last a given number of days

parameterized.parameterized_sql: WITH base AS (SELECT r.observed_at, r.value FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id WHERE s.physical_location = 'Pool' AND s.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.is_active = true AND s.reliable = true AND r.value <= 95 AND r.observed_at >= now() - ($1 * interval '1 day')), windowed AS (SELECT observed_at, value, max(value) OVER w AS max_30min, min(value) OVER w AS min_30min, value - first_value(value) OVER w AS delta_from_start FROM base WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY observed_at RANGE BETWEEN interval '30 minutes' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)), dedup AS (SELECT observed_at, max_30min, min_30min, delta_from_start, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY date_trunc('hour', observed_at) ORDER BY (max_30min - min_30min) DESC) AS rn FROM windowed WHERE (max_30min - min_30min) >= 1.0 AND delta_from_start <= -1.0 AND EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (observed_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles')) BETWEEN 12 AND 19) SELECT (observed_at AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles')::timestamp AS local_time, round(min_30min::numeric,2) AS min_temp_f, round(max_30min::numeric,2) AS max_temp_f, round((max_30min - min_30min)::numeric,2) AS range_f, round(delta_from_start::numeric,2) AS signed_delta_f FROM dedup WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY observed_at DESC LIMIT 50
parameterized.parameterized_intent: Find pool swim events over the last $1 days

templates.nl_query: Show me the daily outdoor high for the last 14 days with the day-to-day change
templates.sql: WITH daily AS (SELECT (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date AS local_day, max(r.value) AS day_max FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id JOIN stations st ON st.mac_address = s.station_id WHERE s.physical_location = 'Outdoor' AND s.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.reliable = true AND r.observed_at >= now() - interval '14 days' GROUP BY 1) SELECT local_day, round(day_max::numeric,1) AS day_max, round((day_max - lag(day_max) OVER (ORDER BY local_day))::numeric,1) AS diff_from_prev FROM daily ORDER BY local_day
templates.intent: Time series of daily outdoor high temperature over the last 14 days with day-to-day change
templates.manifest: Time series of daily maximum a given measurement at a given location over a given window with day-to-day change

parameterized.parameterized_sql: WITH daily AS (SELECT (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date AS local_day, max(r.value) AS day_max FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id JOIN stations st ON st.mac_address = s.station_id WHERE s.physical_location = $1 AND s.measurement_type = $2 AND s.reliable = true AND r.observed_at >= now() - ($3 * interval '1 day') GROUP BY 1) SELECT local_day, round(day_max::numeric,1) AS day_max, round((day_max - lag(day_max) OVER (ORDER BY local_day))::numeric,1) AS diff_from_prev FROM daily ORDER BY local_day
parameterized.parameterized_intent: Time series of daily maximum $2 at $1 for last $3 days with day-to-day change

templates.nl_query: How many times in the last 30 days did the daily outdoor high change by more than 15 degrees?
templates.sql: WITH daily AS (SELECT (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date AS local_day, max(r.value) AS day_max FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id JOIN stations st ON st.mac_address = s.station_id WHERE s.physical_location = 'Outdoor' AND s.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.reliable = true AND r.observed_at >= now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY 1), diffs AS (SELECT local_day, day_max, day_max - lag(day_max) OVER (ORDER BY local_day) AS diff_from_prev FROM daily) SELECT count(*) AS large_swing_count FROM diffs WHERE abs(diff_from_prev) > 15
templates.intent: Count of day-to-day daily-high swings above 15F over the last 30 days for outdoor temperature
templates.manifest: Count of day-to-day changes above a given threshold in daily maximum a given measurement at a given location over a given window

parameterized.parameterized_sql: WITH daily AS (SELECT (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date AS local_day, max(r.value) AS day_max FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id JOIN stations st ON st.mac_address = s.station_id WHERE s.physical_location = $1 AND s.measurement_type = $2 AND s.reliable = true AND r.observed_at >= now() - ($3 * interval '1 day') GROUP BY 1), diffs AS (SELECT local_day, day_max, day_max - lag(day_max) OVER (ORDER BY local_day) AS diff_from_prev FROM daily) SELECT count(*) AS large_swing_count FROM diffs WHERE abs(diff_from_prev) > $4
parameterized.parameterized_intent: Count of day-to-day changes above $4 in daily maximum $2 at $1 over the last $3 days

templates.nl_query: How many days in May 2026 had wind gusts above 20 mph, compared to prior years?
templates.sql: SELECT extract(year FROM r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::int AS yr, count(DISTINCT (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date) AS days_with_event FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id JOIN stations st ON st.mac_address = s.station_id WHERE s.measurement_type = 'wind_gust' AND s.reliable = true AND extract(month FROM r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone) = 5 AND r.value > 20 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
templates.intent: Same-month cross-year comparison of days where a given measurement exceeded a threshold. Note that the earliest complete month of data is Sep 2024; queries for months prior to Aug 2024 will silently return no rows.
templates.manifest: Same-month cross-year comparison of days where a given measurement exceeded a given threshold

parameterized.parameterized_sql: SELECT extract(year FROM r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::int AS yr, count(DISTINCT (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date) AS days_with_event FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id JOIN stations st ON st.mac_address = s.station_id WHERE s.measurement_type = $1 AND s.reliable = true AND extract(month FROM r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone) = $2 AND r.value > $3 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
parameterized.parameterized_intent: Same-month (month = $2) cross-year comparison of days where $1 exceeded $3

templates.nl_query: Are any sensors offline or behind on data?
templates.sql: SELECT s.display_name, s.physical_location, s.measurement_type, s.reliable, s.is_active, max(r.observed_at) AS last_reading_at, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - max(r.observed_at))) / 60 AS minutes_behind FROM sensors s LEFT JOIN sensor_readings r ON r.sensor_id = s.sensor_id WHERE s.is_active = true GROUP BY s.display_name, s.physical_location, s.measurement_type, s.reliable, s.is_active ORDER BY minutes_behind DESC NULLS FIRST
templates.intent: Sensor liveness diagnostic. Lists each active sensor with time since last reading, sorted by staleness. A healthy sensor is within ~10 minutes of now(); anything more than 60 minutes behind is potentially offline. Flags any sensor with reliable=false as well.
templates.manifest: Sensor liveness diagnostic showing time-since-last-reading for each active sensor

parameterized.parameterized_sql: SELECT s.display_name, s.physical_location, s.measurement_type, s.reliable, s.is_active, max(r.observed_at) AS last_reading_at, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - max(r.observed_at))) / 60 AS minutes_behind FROM sensors s LEFT JOIN sensor_readings r ON r.sensor_id = s.sensor_id WHERE s.is_active = true GROUP BY s.display_name, s.physical_location, s.measurement_type, s.reliable, s.is_active ORDER BY minutes_behind DESC NULLS FIRST

templates.nl_query: What time was the hottest temperature today?
templates.sql: SELECT (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::timestamp AS local_time, r.value, s.unit, s.display_name, s.physical_location FROM sensor_readings r JOIN sensors s ON s.sensor_id = r.sensor_id JOIN stations st ON st.mac_address = s.station_id WHERE s.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.reliable = true AND (r.observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date = (now() AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::date ORDER BY r.value DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
templates.intent: Find the peak temperature reading anywhere today (any location) and return it with LOCAL-TIME timestamp plus location. Critical: the SELECT MUST return `(observed_at AT TIME ZONE st.timezone)::timestamp AS local_time` so the natural-language layer never has to convert UTC to local. Returning raw observed_at causes the narrator to speak the UTC hour (e.g. '23:00 UTC' spoken as '11pm last night' when the reading was actually 4pm local today). ALSO include display_name and physical_location so the answer can name the sensor — do NOT return only the station name.
templates.manifest: Find the peak of a given measurement anywhere today, returning local time and sensor identity
